All the states render well. Screenshots under `prototypes/` (live: **http://maker:4001/copy.html?case=page**, and `?case=pdf|capturing|failed|ia-done`).

**A normal page** (`shot-53-copy-page.png`)
Each bookmark keeps a **self-contained page copy** (the whole page saved as one file), shown with when it was saved and its size, plus **View saved copy**, **Download copy**, and **Refresh copy**. The key promise: *"the saved copy opens exactly as it was when you saved it, even if the original later changes or disappears."* The original is still reachable via **Open live page** — the two are distinct.

**A PDF** (`shot-54-copy-pdf.png`)
For a PDF, the **actual PDF file is preserved** (labelled `PDF`, with Download PDF) rather than a page snapshot.

**Internet Archive — optional and explicit** (in every state; `shot-57-copy-ia-done.png` shows it done)
A separate panel lets you **Save a copy to the Internet Archive** when *you* choose to — with an honest note that this sends the page's address to a third-party service. Once done, it shows the date and a **View on web.archive.org** link. It's never automatic.

**When capture can't happen** (`shot-56-copy-failed.png`)
If the page blocks access or is unreachable, it says so plainly and offers **Try again** or **Open the live page instead** — no pretending a copy exists.

Two decisions I need your call on:

1. **When should the local copy be made?** I assumed it's captured **automatically when you save a bookmark** (running in the background, `shot-55-copy-capturing.png`), so you always have one without thinking. The alternative is to keep a copy **only when you ask** per bookmark (lighter on storage). Which do you prefer — always, or on demand?
2. The **Internet Archive** copy stays **opt-in per bookmark** (never automatic). Is that right, or would you want an option to always do it too?
